question.text:
Consider the following two propositions:
$\mathrm{P}_1: \sim(p \rightarrow \sim q)$
$P_2:(p \wedge \sim q) \wedge((\sim p) \vee q)$
If the proposition $p \rightarrow((\sim p) \vee q)$ is evaluated as FALSE, then :

solution.text:
Given propositions $\mathrm{P}_1: \sim(\mathrm{p} \rightarrow \sim \mathrm{q})$
$\mathrm{P}_2:(p \wedge \sim q) \wedge((\sim p) \vee q)$
Required table is shown below.
\(\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|l|l|l|l|l|l|l|}
\hline \mathbf{p} & \mathbf{q} & \sim p & \sim q & \sim p \vee q & p \rightarrow(\sim(p \vee q) & p \rightarrow \sim q & \sim(p \rightarrow \sim q) & p \wedge \sim q & p_2 \\
\hline \text { T } & \text { T } & \text { F } & \text { F } & \text { T } & \text { T } & \text { F } & \text { T } & \text { F } & \text { F } \\
\hline \text { T } & \text { F } & \text { F } & \text { T } & \text { F } & \text { F } & \text { T } & \text { F } & \text { T } & \text { F } \\
\hline \text { F } & \text { T } & \text { T } & \text { F } & \text { T } & \text { T } & \text { T } & \text { F } & \text { F } & \text { F } \\
\hline \text { F } & \text { F } & \text { T } & \text { T } & \text { T } & \text { T } & \text { T } & \text { F } & \text { F } & \text { F } \\
\hline
\end{array}\)
\(p \rightarrow(\sim p \vee q)\) is \(F\) when \(p\) is true \(q\) is false From table \(P_1 ~\&~ P_2\) both are false
